subject: Starlight Health RFI: On‑Prem Egress Controls, Provenance & Upgrade Procedures
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@starlighthealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: On‑Prem deployment controls — egress/provenance/upgrade questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our call last week. As we evaluate Redwood for an on‑prem deployment in our primary datacenter, our security and procurement teams have a short set of follow‑ups focused on network egress controls, request provenance/auditability, and offline upgrade procedures. Please respond to the items below or attach your formal pack.

Key questions: 
- Do you provide a configurable egress allowlist at the control plane and node level? If so, can it be locked to a finite set of IPs/FQDNs and enforced when the environment is air‑gapped?
- How are provenance/audit events captured for inference requests (request id mapping, model version, user/tenant id, and full KV cache events)? Retention and export options?
- Describe offline/airgapped upgrade steps: patch packaging, SBOM availability, signature verification, rollback plan, and expected maintenance window.
- Are there any cloud callbacks required for license validation or telemetry in an air‑gapped install?

Requested deliverables: a short technical Q&A (bullet answers), SBOM export, and a one‑page runbook for on‑prem upgrades. We aim to finalize vendor selections by 11/12.

Thanks — please copy our procurement alias on delivery.

Alice Morgan
Senior IT Procurement
Starlight Health

Attachment: starlight_rfi_template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@starlighthealth.com>
Cc: IT Procurement <procurement@starlighthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:08:34 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: On‑Prem deployment controls — egress/provenance/upgrade questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list.

We put together a concise response pack and attached the files below; highlights inline. If you need deeper evidence or a short tech walkthrough, happy to set up Diego and Soojin to join.

Highlights (short answers):
- Egress allowlist: Yes. Control plane and node‑level allowlists supported. Network policies can be enforced via local firewall rules and our orchestration enforces outbound DNS/IP restrictions. For truly air‑gapped installs, control plane can be run with zero external egress; optional outbound hooks are disabled by default.
- Provenance & audit: Every inference request is stamped with a request_id, model hash, runtime image id, tenant id, and node id. Events are emitted to a local audit store (append‑only) with configurable retention and can be exported as newline JSON or CSV.
- Offline upgrades: We provide signed patch bundles (tar.gpg), a deterministic upgrade tool that verifies signatures, an SBOM ( SPDX/CSV ) for each release, and a documented rollback procedure. Rollback uses snapshotting of model artifacts + runtime image immutability.
- Callbacks/telemetry: No mandatory callbacks required for license or telemetry in air‑gapped mode. Optional telemetry (metrics/health) can be configured to buffer and ship manually via an offline export.

Attached: starlight-onprem-answerpack.pdf (pdf), network-egress-controls.md (md), redwood-sbom-v1.2.csv (csv).

Next steps: Diego/Soogin — can you confirm the SBOM policy for third‑party libs (licensing summary) and the retention defaults for the audit store? Also, can we provide a one‑page runbook for offline upgrades by EOD tomorrow?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:33:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: On‑Prem deployment controls — egress/provenance/upgrade questions

Marissa — quick answers and attached artifacts.

SBOM and licensing: We provide both SPDX (tag‑value) and CSV SBOMs per patch/release. Current release (v1.2) includes one GPLv2 component limited to a build tool that is statically linked; license summary attached (redwood-sbom-v1.2.csv). Legal has approved distribution for air‑gapped installs; commercial exceptions documented in our distro notes.

Audit retention & export: Default retention is 365 days for request/audit events in the local append‑only store. Config is editable at install time (0 = disabled, >0 days allowed). Export formats: newline JSON, CSV, and gzipped tarball of indexed parquet for analytics. Audit events include: timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, model_hash, runtime_image, node_id, kv_cache_events (summary).

Egress controls: network-egress-controls.md attached — we support node local deny/allow rules, and control plane policy enforcement. For air‑gapped installs we ship a hardened installer with egress hooks disabled; outbound certificate revocation checks are disabled unless customer opts in.

Offline upgrade runbook: I drafted the one‑page runbook; attaching to Marissa for final packaging. Expect maintenance window ~20–45 minutes for a single cluster (depends on model cache warm‑up).

Attachments: network-egress-controls.md, redwood-sbom-v1.2.csv, onprem-offline-upgrade-runbook.pdf

— Diego
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: RFI responses: On‑Prem egress & provenance — Starlight pack attached

Alice / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is our consolidated response pack (starlight-onprem-answerpack.pdf) and the raw SBOM + runbook for your review. Summary points below: 

- Egress: Full controllable allowlist at control plane and node level. Air‑gapped installs can be configured with zero external egress; outbound hooks are opt‑in only. See network‑egress controls doc for ports and exact IP/FQDNs required for non‑airgapped optional features.
- Provenance & audit: Local append‑only audit store with 1yr default retention; exports to JSON/CSV/parquet. Events include request_id → model_hash → runtime_image → node mapping.
- Offline upgrades: Signed patch bundles, SBOM included, signature verification and deterministic installer. Typical maintenance window 20–45 minutes per cluster; rollback via snapshot restore.
- Callbacks/Telemetry: Not required. Optional telemetry can be buffered and exported offline.

Please confirm receipt and tell us if you want a short 30‑minute technical walkthrough (we can demo the upgrade flow and show audit exports).

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
